n: In the darkest time of trouble ever known, Michael, the great prince who protects Daniel’s people, will arise. Everyone whose name is written in God’s book will be delivered. Latter-day Saints identify Michael as Adam, who will play a key role in the events of the last days.

f.w: a time of trouble, such as never was

n: One of the clearest Old Testament teachings on resurrection: those who “sleep in the dust” will awake—some to everlasting life, others to shame. Jesus echoed this verse when He taught of the resurrection.

f.w: many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake

n: The wise will shine like the sky, and those who lead others to righteousness will shine like the stars forever. Teaching and helping others toward God has eternal value.

f.w: shine as the brightness of the firmament
they that turn many to righteousness

n: Daniel must seal the book until the time of the end. Then many will travel “to and fro” and knowledge will increase—words many have applied to the explosion of travel, learning, and revealed knowledge in the last days.

f.g: Preserve and secure it, like sealing an important document.

n: Daniel sees two more heavenly beings, one on each bank of the river.
One asks the man clothed in linen, hovering above the waters, “How long until these astonishing things end?”

Raising both hands to heaven—a doubly solemn oath—he swears by the Eternal One: it will be “a time, times, and half a time,” and when the shattering of the holy people is complete, all will be finished.

f.w: held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven
a time, times, and an half
f.g: Probably three and a half “times”—a limited period of tribulation.

n: Daniel honestly admits he doesn’t understand and asks how it will all end. Even prophets don’t always grasp everything they are shown.

f.w: I heard, but I understood not

n: “Go your way, Daniel.” The words are sealed until the end—their full meaning will be understood later.

f.w: the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end

n: Many will be purified and refined through trial, but the wicked will continue in evil and won’t understand. Only the wise will understand—spiritual insight depends on the heart.

f.w: purified, and made white, and tried

n: From the ending of the daily sacrifice and the setting up of the abomination will be 1,290 days—about three and a half years with an added month.
A blessing for the one who waits patiently and reaches 1,335 days. The varying numbers may mark stages; the main lesson is faithful endurance.

A tender ending for the aged prophet: go your way; you will rest in death, and at the end of days you will rise to receive your allotted inheritance. Daniel’s faithful life ends with the promise of resurrection.

f.w: stand in thy lot at the end of the days
f.g: Rise to receive your inheritance (lot = allotted portion).
